text:
eva: Heads up — starting ~09:10 UTC we saw a sharp drop in prefix cache hit rate for the prod serving tier. Backend RPS to model-pool-4 spiked ~3x and a few endpoints started returning 503s. Paging because this looks like a cache-induced backpressure event.

matt: Oof. Any idea what changed recently? rollout? kernel config?

eva: no rollout on the runtime in the last 24h besides the scheduled kernel-selector tweak yesterday morning. attaching quick metrics: hit-rate dropped from 87% -> 21% around 09:10, latency p50 x3.

olga: can you paste the query that shows hit-rate? also curious if hot-keys concentrated on a small set of prefixes.

eva: sure — from monitoring: 
```
SELECT time_bucket('1m', ts) AS minute, sum(hit)::float / sum(req) AS hit_rate
FROM prefix_cache.metrics
WHERE cluster = 'prod' AND pool = 'model-pool-4' AND ts > now() - interval '2 hours'
GROUP BY minute
ORDER BY minute;
```

rahul: i dug into request traces — 90% of misses were for ~120 hot prefixes (customer prompts) that have long contexts; seems the cache keying stripped session metadata yesterday due to a change in the key-hash salt. if salt changed, old cached values are invisible -> mass miss.

matt: ah, keying drift. that explains the stampede-like traffic to upstream. are we certain the salt changed? which PR?

rahul: PR #4321 in runtime-config bumped the key-salt to include model-version for an experiment; it was toggled on by default. seemed harmless but it fragmented keys.

olga: ok. options: 1) roll back the key-salt change 2) emergency enable a compatibility path that checks legacy-key before miss bounce 3) throttle prefetch/batching to reduce load. i'm leaning to (2) + (3) short-term to avoid rollback.

sara: i'm +1 for compatibility path first. rollback is risky during business hours. we should also reduce batch size for that pool to keep latency bounded.

kb-deploy-bot: eva requested: toggle runtime.flag.kv_legacy_lookup=true in prod clusters (model-pool-4). Action queued.

kb-deploy-bot: action complete: runtime.flag.kv_legacy_lookup=true applied to model-pool-4 (3/3 hosts) — 09:32 UTC.

eva: after legacy lookup enabled, hit-rate rose from 21% -> 65% within 8 minutes. error rate dropped. still below baseline though.

matt: good. can we also temporarily reduce max_batch_tokens for pool-4? command?

olga: yes — runtime.admin.update_pool_config(pool='model-pool-4', max_batch_tokens=512) — did it manually, change propagated 09:45.

rahul: quick note: kernel-selector experiment also changed operator that prunes KV entries on long sequences; that might have accelerated eviction for these hot keys. logs show increased eviction churn around the same time. need to revert that behavior in the next patch.

eva: putting an incident anchor: https://internal-graphs/redwood/prod/prefix-cache/hitrate?range=2h (internal) — flamegraph shows heavy time in network and kv-serialize during the surge.

matt: action items: 
- rahul to strip model-version from key-salt in config (or gate behind feature flag) 
- olga to add a compatibility lookup path test to CI (covers legacy -> new key)
- infra to add a short-circuit rate limiter when miss-rate > 40% for a pool (prevents cascade)
- product to notify impacted customers if we see continued errors

sara: i'm creating a short postmortem template for this (will include timeline + mitigations). prioritize root cause: keying change + eviction churn + no cascade limiter.

eva: current status 10:05 UTC — hit-rate 78%, errors back near baseline, RPS normalized. leaving legacy lookup enabled while we prepare a safer rollout path.

olga: follow-ups: add canary checks around key-hash changes, add a metric for "legacy-lookup-fallbacks" and make it alert if >5% of hits are fallbacks. also add a staged rollout for keying changes.

rahul: i'll open PR to gate the key-salt change behind an opt-in flag and include migration logic that backfills keys for hot prefixes.

matt: great. when we write the postmortem, call out that kernel-selector and eviction heuristics were amplifiers not root cause — the primary was key fragmentation.

eva: one-liner for ops log: "09:10 UTC — keying schema change caused prefix cache fragmentation -> miss storm -> backend overload; mitigated by enabling legacy-lookup, throttling batch size, and applying short-term pool-level rate limiting."

kb-deploy-bot: Note: scheduled rollback window for runtime.flag.kv_legacy_lookup=false on 1801244167 unless changed by owner.

sara: tagging for follow-up: @oncall-eng @perf-team @prod-eng. I'll draft the incident postmortem and ping for review. :white_check_mark:
